intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, matcha sweets, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture in Akihabara. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, visit retro game shops, explore maid cafes, and discover the latest gadgets and robotics displays. A must-do for anyone fascinated by Japan's cutting-edge consumer tech scene.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, at dawn before the crowds arrive. Stroll through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, explore the surrounding Asakusa district's rickshaws, geisha districts, and old Edo-era architecture for a deep cultural experience.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and culture converge. TeamLab Borderless features immersive, interactive rooms where art moves and transforms around visitors, blending Japanese aesthetics with cutting-edge projection and sensor technology for a truly unforgettable experience.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Izakaya Hopping & Ramen Alley
experiences.description: Spend an evening exploring Shinjuku's legendary Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane), hopping between tiny izakayas serving yakitori, sake, and craft Japanese whisky. Cap the night with a steaming bowl of tonkotsu or shoyu ramen from one of the atmospheric alley stalls beloved by locals and chefs alike.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or train (Narita Express or Keikyu Line) to Tsukiji area. Check in to Tsukiji boutique stay, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tsukiji Outer Market stalls for an early dinner — try fresh tamagoyaki (egg rolls), grilled scallops, and tuna skewers from street vendors. Walk to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens entrance for a sunset view of the gardens and Tokyo skyline (entry ¥300). Return to hotel and rest to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick convenience store bento (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the station for ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market street food stalls — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a filling mix of skewers, sushi bites, and tamagoyaki

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Load ¥3,000–¥5,000 to start. Keep receipts — Japan is largely cash-based so withdraw yen at the airport 7-Eleven ATM which accepts foreign cards.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00 AM) to visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its liveliest. Browse fresh seafood, pickles, knives, and kitchenware shops. Enjoy a classic breakfast of fresh sushi or a sashimi bowl (kaisendon) from one of the market's iconic breakfast spots like Sushi Dai queue alternative stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Ginza (one stop away). Window-shop Tokyo's luxury district for free — admire the architecture of the Itoya stationery flagship store and the Apple Store. Head to the free observation floor of the Ginza Six rooftop garden. Then walk to the free Advertising Museum Tokyo (ADMT) in Shiodome to see Japan's tech-meets-culture advertising history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome's Caretta shopping complex for the free illumination displays (seasonal). Dinner at the basement food halls (depachika) of a nearby department store for affordable set meals. Return to Tsukiji by foot or subway.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Ginza side-street shop — ¥900–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Depachika (department store basement) bento or hot food counter — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant before 9 AM. The inner wholesale market has relocated to Toyosu but the outer market remains tourist-friendly and delicious. Ginza is free to explore — avoid buying anything to stay on budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and tech/otaku culture hub. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera (free entry). Browse retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and maid café flyers. Visit the free floors of Akihabara Radio Kaikan building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deeper into Akihabara's tech culture — visit Super Potato retro game store (free to browse), Animate manga/anime store, and the Gundam Café area. Head to the nearby 2k540 AKI-OKA ARTISAN craft market under the elevated train tracks (free entry) for a look at Japanese artisan tech and design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner at a budget chain restaurant — try Matsuya or Yoshinoya gyudon (beef bowl) for ¥500–¥700. Then experience one affordable maid café session (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 minimum charge) for a quintessential Akihabara cultural experience. Return to Tsukiji via Hibiya or Asakusa line.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and coffee from FamilyMart near hotel — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen or curry shop — ¥800–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Gyudon beef bowl at Matsuya or Yoshinoya — ¥500–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored slowly — many shops have multiple floors. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout. Friday evenings can be crowded with after-work crowds adding to the energy. The maid café experience is optional but culturally iconic.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry) early morning when crowds are lighter. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, and ningyoyaki snacks. Ring the temple bell and explore the five-story pagoda grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River to the Tokyo Skytree base area (exterior viewing and shopping mall free). Visit the Sumida Hokusai Museum (¥400 entry) for stunning ukiyo-e woodblock print art. Cross back over the Azuma Bridge for a classic Tokyo photo of Skytree and the Asahi Beer Hall golden flame sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Hoppy Street (Hoppy-dori) for budget izakaya dining — try yakitori skewers, oden, and hoppy beer (a low-alcohol budget drink). The street is lively on Saturday evenings. Return to hotel via the Asakusa subway line.

meals.breakfast: Ningyo-yaki cakes and taiyaki fish-shaped pastry from Nakamise Street stalls — ¥200–¥400
meals.lunch: Asakusa soba noodles at a local shop — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya — ¥1,200–¥1,800 for skewers, small plates, and a drink

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free and spectacular. Saturday crowds can be heavy by mid-morning so arrive before 9 AM. The Sumida Hokusai Museum is a hidden gem and very affordable. Hoppy Street is a beloved local budget dining tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Harajuku — arrive at Meiji Jingu Shrine early (free entry). Walk the forested gravel path through towering torii gates to the main shrine. Participate in a free traditional prayer ritual. The forest walk takes about 20 minutes each way and is peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's wild street fashion culture (free to browse). Try a budget crepe from one of the many crepe stands (¥400–¥600). Then walk through Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's tree-lined Champs-Élysées — for free architecture and people-watching. Visit the free Omotesando Hills atrium.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Shibuya. Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing from the free second-floor viewing window at Starbucks (buy a ¥500 coffee for a seat) or from the free Mag's Park rooftop at Shibuya 109-2. Dinner at a Shibuya side-street izakaya or conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Kura Sushi.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe + onigiri from a nearby konbini — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Kura Sushi conveyor belt sushi in Shibuya — ¥1,000–¥1,500 (¥110–¥165 per plate)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is especially beautiful in spring — cherry blossoms may still be visible in mid-April. Harajuku is most vibrant on Sundays. Shibuya Scramble is best viewed at dusk or after dark when neon signs are lit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the TeamLab Planets digital art museum in Toyosu (book tickets in advance online — ¥3,200). This is a splurge day for tech-meets-art culture. The immersive digital art experience is one of Tokyo's most iconic modern attractions and worth the budget stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the Toyosu Market area (the relocated inner fish market). Visit the free observation decks overlooking the tuna auction floor (no longer active for tourists but the market infrastructure is viewable). Take the free Yurikamome monorail scenic ride from Toyosu toward Odaiba for skyline views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Odaiba — visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza exterior with its giant Unicorn Gundam statue (a tech culture icon). Walk along the Odaiba waterfront for views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Dinner at the Aqua City Odaiba food court for affordable options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area konbini breakfast — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market area seafood bowl or sushi set — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Odaiba Aqua City food court — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Planets must be booked online in advance — walk-in tickets are rarely available. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting slightly wet in the water installation rooms. The Yurikamome monorail pass can be bought as a day pass for ¥820 — worth it if you ride multiple times.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Ueno. Visit Ueno Park (free entry) — one of Tokyo's best cherry blossom parks (late blooms may still be visible in mid-April). Walk through the park past Shinobazu Pond and the outdoor sculptures. Visit the free exterior of the Tokyo National Museum and the Toshogu Shrine within the park (¥200 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ameyoko Market — a bustling open-air street market under the elevated train tracks near Ueno Station. Browse cheap snacks, dried seafood, clothing, and cosmetics. Great for budget souvenir shopping. Then walk to nearby Yanaka Ginza — a beautifully preserved old Tokyo shotengai (shopping street) with local shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Yanaka neighborhood at a local shokudo (casual Japanese diner) for home-style Japanese cooking at very affordable prices. Explore the Yanaka Cemetery at dusk — a peaceful, atmospheric old Tokyo neighborhood. Return to Tsukiji via subway.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and canned coffee from a Ueno area konbini — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — takoyaki, yakitori, fresh fruit — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Yanaka Ginza local shokudo set meal (teishoku) — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free and massive — allow at least 2 hours to walk through properly. Ameyoko is one of Tokyo's best budget shopping streets. Yanaka is one of the few neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing and retains old Showa-era Tokyo charm — a cultural highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Shinjuku. Start at the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (North Tower — free, opens 9:30 AM) for panoramic 360-degree views of Tokyo including Mt. Fuji on clear days. This is the best free city view in Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially stunning if late cherry blossoms or spring flowers remain. Then explore the Shinjuku Kabukicho entertainment district for its architecture and street energy (free to walk through). Visit the free Robot Restaurant street-level exterior and the Golden Gai alley district.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's Golden Gai — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars each holding 5–8 people. Many have a small cover charge (¥500–¥1,000) but drinks are affordable. Choose one bar for an authentic local Tokyo nightlife experience. Dinner at Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for grilled yakitori skewers in a smoky, nostalgic alley.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku konbini or bakery near the government building — ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen park picnic with konbini bento — ¥600–¥800
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori skewers — ¥1,200–¥1,800 for a full meal with beer

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is one of the best free activities in all of Tokyo — go on a clear morning for Mt. Fuji views. Golden Gai bars are tiny and intimate — respect the space and be friendly. Some bars are locals-only but most welcome tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji neighborhood — a beloved Tokyo counterculture hub known for vintage shops, indie music, and local art. Explore the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) and browse vintage clothing shops. Koenji is a favorite among Tokyo's creative and tech-adjacent subculture community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nakameguro — walk along the Meguro River canal (especially beautiful with remaining spring foliage). Browse the boutique shops and independent cafés along the canal. Visit the free Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural space beloved by Tokyo's design community.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ebisu and visit the Yebisu Beer Museum (free entry, tastings optional at ¥400 for two samples). Then explore the Ebisu Garden Place shopping complex (free) for its European-inspired architecture. Dinner at an affordable Ebisu or Nakameguro local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Koenji local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) breakfast set — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Nakameguro canal-side café sandwich or rice bowl — ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Ebisu area budget ramen or curry restaurant — ¥800–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Koenji and Nakameguro represent Tokyo's creative class culture — very different from the tourist trail. Daikanyama T-Site is architecturally stunning and free to browse. The Meguro River walk is one of Tokyo's most photogenic spots in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) on Odaiba (¥630 entry) — one of the world's best science and technology museums. See ASIMO robot demonstrations, interactive AI exhibits, and a stunning geodesic sphere displaying real-time Earth data. A must for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Miraikan, walk to the nearby Palette Town area (free) to see the giant ferris wheel exterior and the Toyota Mega Web showroom (free) showcasing futuristic Toyota concept cars and driving simulators. Then visit the teamLab Borderless site area (exterior) or the nearby free VenusFort shopping mall.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Yurikamome monorail back toward central Tokyo. Stop at Shiodome for dinner at the affordable Caretta Shiodome food floors. Walk back to Tsukiji along the Sumida River waterfront for a beautiful evening city view.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji area konbini — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court or DiverCity Tokyo restaurant — ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Caretta Shiodome food floor set meal — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is exceptional for tech culture lovers — the ASIMO demonstrations have set times so check the schedule at the entrance. Toyota Mega Web is completely free and surprisingly impressive with concept cars and a test track. Book Miraikan tickets online to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (about 2 hours from Tokyo via Tobu Nikko Line — budget ¥1,360 each way from Asakusa). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrine complexes set in a cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Rinno-ji Temple and the Futarasan Shrine. If time permits, walk along the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (¥300 to cross). Explore the cedar-lined Nikko National Park paths. Nikko combines Japan's traditional culture, nature, and architectural grandeur in one place.
day_by_day.evening: Return train to Tokyo by late afternoon/early evening. Arrive back at Tsukiji area by 7–8 PM. Dinner at a local Tsukiji sushi restaurant or Ginza area budget sushi counter. Early night to rest after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben (train station bento box) at Asakusa Station — ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a local restaurant near the shrine — ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area standing sushi bar — ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa is the cheapest way to reach Nikko. Buy a Nikko World Heritage Pass (¥2,200) which covers entry to the main shrine complex and saves money over individual tickets. Nikko is Japan's most elaborately decorated shrine area — allow at least 4 hours on site.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, indie theaters, and café culture. Sunday mornings are perfect here. Browse the dozens of secondhand clothing and vinyl record shops. This neighborhood represents Tokyo's creative underground culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sangenjaya neighborhood nearby — another local favorite with a labyrinthine covered shopping arcade called Sangen-jaya Triangle. Explore the local shotengai markets and small independent shops. Visit a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) for afternoon coffee and cake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo for a final major evening experience. Visit Roppongi Hills Mori Art Museum (¥2,000 entry, includes observation deck) for contemporary art and one of Tokyo's best 360-degree night panoramas from the 52nd floor. This is a splurge-worthy final evening cultural highlight. Dinner in Roppongi at an affordable ramen or tonkatsu restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa local bakery or kissaten morning set — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Sangenjaya local teishoku set lunch — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Roppongi tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,400

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best on Sunday when the flea markets and vintage shops are fully open. The Mori Art Museum stays open until 10 PM on Sundays — perfect for a night visit when the Tokyo panorama is most spectacular. This is a great penultimate day combining local culture and a memorable high point.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji — revisit the Outer Market for a farewell sushi breakfast. Buy any last-minute food souvenirs: dried seaweed, Japanese tea, tamagoyaki pans, or quality chopsticks at market prices. Walk to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) for a peaceful final stroll through this beautiful traditional garden with Tokyo skyscrapers as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to hotel to check out and collect luggage. Take the train or bus to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow at least 3–4 hours before your flight for travel time and check-in. At the airport, browse the duty-free shops and pick up last-minute gifts like Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito, or Kit Kat Japanese flavors.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If flight is late evening, enjoy one final airport ramen or soba at the airport food court — Japanese airport food is genuinely good and affordable.

meals.breakfast: Farewell sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Light konbini snacks or airport food court — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Airport ramen or soba before departure — ¥800–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at the nearest train station (¥400–¥600) if you want a few more hours to explore. The Narita Express (N'EX) from Shinjuku takes about 90 minutes to Narita Airport — budget ¥3,070 one way. Haneda is closer and cheaper via Keikyu Line (¥300–¥400, 30 minutes from central Tokyo).

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to boutique hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market (仲見世通り), which stays lively into the afternoon. Browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki shops, and kitchen supply vendors to get your first taste of Tokyo street life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens for a peaceful evening walk along the tidal pond — entry is ¥300. Watch the city lights begin to glow over Tokyo Bay. Return to Tsukiji for dinner at a local sushi or seafood izakaya to celebrate arrival.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a convenience store onigiri and green tea at 7-Eleven near the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack at Tsukiji Outer Market — try grilled scallops or fresh tuna skewers from market stalls (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai (寿司三昧) on Tsukiji — a beloved mid-range sushi chain open late, budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be strong — keep Day 1 light. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport to use on all trains and buses throughout the trip. April is cherry blossom season so expect some crowds at parks.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (jet lag works in your favor!) and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at 7:00 AM for a legendary breakfast — fresh uni, toro, and tamago on rice bowls at market stalls. This is the authentic local food experience Tokyo is famous for.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (秋葉原), Tokyo's electric town and tech culture hub. Explore multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera, retro game stores, anime merchandise shops, and maid cafés. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center for vintage electronics nostalgia.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner then explore the neon-lit streets after dark. Visit a multi-story arcade like Club Sega or Taito Station for a uniquely Japanese gaming experience.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast bowls — Donburi Ichiba or Nakagawa — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.lunch: Ramen at Akihabara's Fuunji or a nearby tonkotsu ramen shop — budget ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) at a mid-range spot in Akihabara — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored slowly — allow at least 3–4 hours. Many shops open at 10:00 AM. Free Wi-Fi available in most electronics stores.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple (浅草寺) in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive by 8:00 AM to beat crowds. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, and folding fans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Asakusa's backstreets and the Kappabashi Kitchenware Street (合羽橋道具街) — a fascinating street lined with professional cooking supply shops, plastic food sample makers, and knife specialists. A must for food culture lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Tokyo Mizube Cruising Line water bus from Asakusa Pier to Odaiba (~¥780). Enjoy views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline at dusk. Explore Odaiba's futuristic waterfront and the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ~¥3,200).

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a kissaten (old-school café) near Senso-ji — budget ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa — a 120-year-old institution, budget ¥1,800–¥2,500
meals.dinner: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza food court in Odaiba for a variety of Japanese options — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online in advance — check availability before the trip. The water bus ride is a scenic and unique way to travel across Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shibuya (渋谷) to see the famous Scramble Crossing — best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation deck above. Visit Shibuya Sky (渋谷スカイ) rooftop observation deck for 360° city views (¥2,000, book ahead).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku (原宿) — walk Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and crepes, then transition to the elegant Omotesando (表参道) boulevard for architecture, design boutiques, and the Prada/Louis Vuitton flagship stores designed by famous architects.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omotesando or Aoyama, then evening drinks at a rooftop bar in Shibuya. The area is vibrant on Saturday nights.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast from FamilyMart or Lawson near hotel — onigiri, coffee, and a pastry — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Afuri Ramen in Harajuku — known for yuzu shio ramen, budget ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Gyukatsu Motomura in Shibuya — famous beef cutlet restaurant, budget ¥1,800–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means crowds in Harajuku and Shibuya — arrive at Takeshita Street before noon if possible. Omotesando Hills mall is worth a peek for its architecture by Tadao Ando.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (明治神宮) in Harajuku — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Sunday mornings often feature traditional wedding processions. The forested path is peaceful and beautiful in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Shinjuku (新宿). Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑, ¥500) — one of Japan's best cherry blossom viewing spots, with French, English, and Japanese garden sections. Perfect for a relaxed Sunday afternoon picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shinjuku's neon-lit Kabukicho entertainment district and the famous Golden Gai (ゴールデン街) — a labyrinth of tiny themed bars each seating just 6–10 people. Perfect for experiencing Tokyo's unique nightlife culture.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a Doutor or Komeda's Coffee near the hotel — budget ¥500–¥900
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen — pick up bento boxes from a convenience store or depachika (department store basement food hall) — budget ¥800–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — tiny yakitori stalls under the train tracks, budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays. Golden Gai bars are tiny and intimate — most welcome tourists but check for signs. Bring cash as many small bars don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (日光) — take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (~2 hours, ~¥1,400). Visit Tosho-gu Shrine (東照宮), a UNESCO World Heritage Site with ornate gold-leaf carvings and the famous 'See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil' monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's sacred complex — visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate, and Futarasan Shrine. Walk through the cedar-lined Cryptomeria Avenue. The mountain air and greenery are refreshing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Rest and recover at the hotel or have a quiet dinner near Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel or konbini before early departure
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a local Nikko restaurant — a regional specialty, budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Simple soba or udon at a neighborhood restaurant near Tsukiji — budget ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Nikko All Area Pass from Tobu Railway for unlimited rides and shrine discounts (~¥4,520). Start early — aim to be on the train by 8:00 AM. Nikko is particularly beautiful in April with fresh greenery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (江戸東京博物館) in Ryogoku — an outstanding museum documenting Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern times. Scale models, artifacts, and interactive displays make it fascinating for culture lovers (¥600).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Ryogoku Kokugikan Sumo Arena (国技館) — check if there's a sumo tournament (basho) in April; if so, purchase tickets for the afternoon session. If no tournament, visit the Sumo Museum inside (free). Explore the sumo stable neighborhood nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Sumida River and explore the Kiyosumi-Shirakawa (清澄白河) neighborhood — Tokyo's specialty coffee culture hub. Browse independent coffee roasters and the Tokyo Museum of Contemporary Art (東京都現代美術館).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a morning café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Chankonabe (sumo stew) at a restaurant near Ryogoku — hearty and authentic, budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Craft coffee and light dinner at a Kiyosumi-Shirakawa café-restaurant — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: The January, May, and September sumo tournaments are held in Ryogoku — April does not have a Tokyo basho, but the museum and stable walks are still worthwhile. Check the official schedule for any special events.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets (チームラボ プラネッツ) in Toyosu — an immersive digital art museum where you walk through water and light installations barefoot (¥3,200, book online). A completely unique sensory experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market (豊洲市場) — the world's largest fish market, relocated from Tsukiji in 2018. Take the observation deck tour to watch the famous tuna auction (lottery registration required weeks in advance) or simply explore the market building and its excellent seafood restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short trip to Ginza (銀座) — Tokyo's most upscale shopping and dining district. Window shop at flagship stores, visit the Itoya stationery store (a 12-floor stationery wonderland), and enjoy the elegant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Konbini or light café breakfast before heading to teamLab
meals.lunch: Sushi or seafood bowl at Toyosu Market's restaurant floor — budget ¥2,000–¥3,500
meals.dinner: Ginza Six basement food hall (depachika) for gourmet takeaway, or a mid-range Japanese restaurant in Ginza — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets is different from Borderless — both are worth visiting if budget allows. Toyosu tuna auction observation requires advance lottery registration on the Toyosu Market website. Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji (~15 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation — Miraikan (日本科学未来館) on Odaiba. This world-class science museum covers robotics, AI, space exploration, and internet technology. Meet ASIMO or similar robots in demonstrations (¥630).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sony ExploraScience exhibits or the nearby Panasonic Center Tokyo — both showcase cutting-edge consumer technology and innovation. This is the tech culture deep dive of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo and visit the Roppongi (六本木) arts district. The Mori Art Museum (森美術館) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower offers both world-class contemporary art and the Tokyo City View observation deck (¥2,000 combined ticket, open until midnight).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café
meals.lunch: Restaurant inside Miraikan or Odaiba's DiverCity food options — budget ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Roppongi Hills restaurant complex — try a mid-range Japanese or fusion restaurant — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. The Mori Art Museum stays open until midnight on Wednesdays and weekends — perfect for an evening visit. Roppongi also has the National Art Center Tokyo (free admission to building) nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (鎌倉) — take the JR Yokosuka Line from Shinagawa (~1 hour, ~¥920). Visit the Great Buddha of Kotoku-in (高徳院, ¥300) — a 13-meter bronze statue dating to 1252. Then explore Hase-dera Temple with its sea views and hydrangea gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and crafts. Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through the forested hills connecting Kamakura's temples. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Optional: stop in Yokohama's Chinatown for dinner on the way back (add 20 minutes to journey).

meals.breakfast: Early konbini breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Shirasu don (whitebait rice bowl) at a Kamakura restaurant — a local specialty, budget ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Yokohama Chinatown dim sum or ramen — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500, or simple dinner near hotel

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is best enjoyed on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Wear comfortable shoes for temple hiking. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line if you have one. April weather in Kamakura is mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館) in Ueno Park (上野公園) — Japan's largest museum with over 110,000 artifacts including samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient pottery (¥1,000). Ueno Park itself is beautiful in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yanaka (谷中) — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander Yanaka Ginza shopping street, visit old temples, and browse artisan workshops. This is authentic old Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ueno's Ameyoko Market (アメ横) — a bustling open-air market street with street food, discount goods, and lively vendors. Then enjoy dinner in the Ueno or Akihabara area.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel
meals.lunch: Menchi katsu (deep-fried meat cutlet) or cream puffs from Yanaka Ginza street stalls — budget ¥500–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Ueno or Akihabara — try a variety of small plates with beer or sake — budget ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Yanaka is best explored without a map — getting slightly lost is part of the charm. Bring cash for Ameyoko Market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Shiodome and Shimbashi area — explore the Panasonic Shiodome Museum of Art and the retro Shimbashi SL Plaza with its preserved steam locomotive. Walk along the Shiodome skybridge for views of Hamarikyu Gardens and Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hamarikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園, ¥300) for a proper visit — enjoy the traditional teahouse on the pond for matcha and wagashi sweets (¥510). Reflect on the trip in this beautiful Edo-period garden surrounded by modern skyscrapers.
day_by_day.evening: Final big shopping run — visit Ginza or the Mitsukoshi Department Store for Japanese gifts, food souvenirs (omiyage), and last-minute purchases. Head to the Tsukiji Outer Market area for a final farewell dinner at your favorite spot.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a kissaten (retro Japanese café) morning set
meals.lunch: Matcha sweets and light snacks at Hamarikyu's Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse — budget ¥600–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Splurge farewell dinner — omakase sushi at a mid-range Tsukiji restaurant or Ginza sushi counter — budget ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to buy omiyage (souvenir gifts) — Tokyo Banana, Royce chocolate, and Yoku Moku cookies are popular choices available at Ginza Mitsukoshi. Hamarikyu teahouse requires a small additional fee on top of garden admission.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast. Pack and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at the nearest subway station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time — light exploration of the Nihonbashi (日本橋) area, Tokyo's historic commercial heart. Visit Coredo Muromachi for Japanese craft goods and the Mitsukoshi Nihonbashi flagship store (Japan's oldest department store). Cross the historic Nihonbashi Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport — allow 2–3 hours before flight departure. Take the Narita Express from Tokyo Station or the Limousine Bus from Ginza/Tsukiji area.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — splurge on the best tuna bowl you can find — budget ¥2,000–¥3,500
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nihonbashi Coredo food hall or airport terminal restaurants — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — try the terminal ramen or soba for a final Japanese meal

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan airport transfer accordingly — Narita is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo, Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Coin lockers are available at most major stations. Reclaim consumption tax refunds at the airport tax refund counters before check-in if you made eligible purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, matcha sweets, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Engage with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated stalls for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to boutique hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City via private airport limousine service (pre-booked luxury transfer, approx. 60–90 min depending on traffic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and freshen up at the boutique hotel. Once settled (around 15:00–16:00), take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market lanes to get your bearings — browse the artisan knife shops, dried seafood stalls, and specialty condiment vendors. Pick up a light snack of fresh tamagoyaki or premium sushi rolls from a top vendor to ease into Tokyo's food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first dinner close to the hotel in the Tsukiji/Ginza area. Head to Ginza (10-minute taxi) for a refined kaiseki or omakase sushi experience to begin the trip on a high culinary note. Afterward, take a night stroll along Ginza's illuminated luxury boulevard before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport meal before arrival)
meals.lunch: Light snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market upon arrival — fresh oysters, tamagoyaki skewers, and matcha soft-serve from premium market stalls
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at Sushi Saito annex or Ginza Kyubey (Ginza) — world-class Edo-mae sushi with seasonal toppings; reserve well in advance; budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book private airport transfer. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul flight. April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — Tsukiji riverside may have late-blooming sakura along the Sumida River banks.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (guided premium experience, 08:00–10:30): Explore the bustling market with a knowledgeable local guide, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, matcha sweets, uni, and street snacks. Visit specialty vendors for premium dashi, rare teas, and artisan knives. This is the quintessential Tsukiji experience right at your doorstep.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Hamarikyu Gardens (10-minute walk from Tsukiji) — a stunning feudal-era garden with a traditional teahouse on a tidal pond. Enjoy a formal matcha tea ceremony in the Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse surrounded by manicured gardens and seasonal flowers. Afterward, take the Tokyo Water Bus (Sumida River cruise) north toward Asakusa for a scenic river journey through old Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Senso-ji Temple at dusk when crowds thin and lanterns glow beautifully. Browse the Nakamise shopping street for premium souvenirs — lacquerware, silk goods, and traditional crafts. Dinner in Asakusa at a high-end tempura restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick market bite at Tsukiji before the tour begins — fresh tuna sashimi rice bowl (maguro don) at Tsukiji's Yonehana
meals.lunch: Tasting bites accumulated during the Tsukiji Food Tour count as a substantial late breakfast/brunch; supplement with a bowl of premium ramen at Tsukiji Kagura nearby
meals.dinner: Tempura Daikokuya (Asakusa) — historic restaurant serving perfectly fried seasonal tempura in a traditional setting; or Kaminarimon Sukeroku for refined kaiseki; budget ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant 07:00–10:00. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Hamarikyu Gardens entry fee is nominal. Book the Nakajima no Ochaya matcha ceremony in advance. Water Bus tickets can be purchased at the pier.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and tech/anime culture hub (20 minutes by subway from Tsukiji). Begin with a deep dive into multi-story electronics megastores: Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera for the latest Japanese gadgets, robotics, and tech innovations unavailable elsewhere. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for specialty electronics and rare components.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akihabara's otaku culture layer: visit Super Potato (retro gaming paradise), Kotobukiya (premium collectibles and figures), and browse maid cafés for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience. Head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda — a repurposed school turned cutting-edge contemporary art and tech-art space showcasing Japanese digital artists and innovators.
day_by_day.evening: Move to the upscale Marunouchi/Tokyo Station area for dinner. Visit the KITTE building's rooftop terrace for views of Tokyo Station's historic red-brick facade. Dine at one of the premium restaurants inside KITTE or the adjacent Marunouchi Building.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Tsukiji morning bowl — try Sushi Zanmai near the market for a fresh tuna breakfast set
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a themed high-concept restaurant — try the Robot Restaurant area or a high-quality ramen shop like Fuunji (nearby Shinjuku style); alternatively, a refined tonkatsu set at Maisen Akihabara branch
meals.dinner: Tableaux or Signatures restaurant in Marunouchi — contemporary French-Japanese fusion with panoramic Tokyo views; or Steakhouse Yoshida for premium Japanese Wagyu A5 Kobe beef course; budget ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Friday afternoons can be busy. Consider purchasing a Suica card for seamless subway travel. April evenings can be cool — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit TeamLab Borderless or TeamLab Planets (Toyosu, 15 minutes from Tsukiji) — Tokyo's world-famous immersive digital art museums where technology and art merge into breathtaking interactive experiences. Book the first entry slot (09:00 or 10:00) to avoid weekend crowds. TeamLab represents the pinnacle of Japan's art-tech fusion culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the futuristic Toyosu area and the nearby Toyosu Market observation deck (the professional wholesale fish market that succeeded Tsukiji's inner market) — watch the inner workings of Tokyo's seafood supply chain from glass-enclosed observation galleries. Return toward central Tokyo and visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills for contemporary Japanese and international art.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roppongi for the evening. Visit the Tokyo City View observation deck atop Mori Tower at sunset for panoramic 360° views of the city. Dinner in Roppongi's upscale dining district.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a high-quality depachika (department store basement food hall) — try Isetan or Mitsukoshi Ginza for premium onigiri, pastries, and Japanese breakfast sets
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch near Toyosu Market — Itadori or Sushizanmai Toyosu for ultra-fresh market-quality sushi at competitive prices given the proximity to the source
meals.dinner: Roppongi Hills Club or Azabu Juban's Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) for an extraordinary omakase experience; alternatively, The Dining at Roppongi Hills for a sophisticated multi-course Japanese-French menu; budget ¥35,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab tickets must be booked online well in advance — Saturday slots sell out weeks ahead. Toyosu Market observation is free but check operational hours (closed Wednesdays and some Sundays). Mori Art Museum is open late on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander the narrow lanes of Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent galleries, artisan workshops, and century-old temples. Visit the serene Yanaka Cemetery, famous for its sakura trees and the graves of notable historical figures including the last Tokugawa shogun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Move to Ueno Park — Japan's premier cultural precinct. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (the largest art museum in Japan) to explore its extraordinary collection of Japanese antiquities, samurai armor, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Stroll through Ueno Park's remaining cherry blossom trees and visit Shinobazu Pond's lotus garden.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic mercantile heart and one of the city's most elegant neighborhoods. Explore the beautifully restored Coredo Muromachi complex for premium Japanese goods, sake, and artisan crafts. Dinner at a traditional kappo (counter-style) restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast set at the hotel or a neighborhood kissaten (old-school Tokyo coffee shop) near Tsukiji — try Chatei Hatou style café for a premium hand-drip coffee and morning toast
meals.lunch: Yanaka area lunch — try Yanaka Beer Hall for craft beers and Japanese pub food, or a traditional soba restaurant like Yabu Soba (Ueno area) for hand-cut buckwheat noodles in a historic setting; budget ¥3,000–¥5,000
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi Yukari (3 Michelin stars) — exquisite kaiseki cuisine celebrating Japanese seasonal ingredients in an intimate, refined setting; or Hamacho Kaneko for premium traditional Japanese cuisine; budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored slowly on foot — allow 2–3 hours. Tokyo National Museum is closed Mondays but open Sundays. Consider purchasing a museum combination ticket for savings across Ueno's multiple museums.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Shibuya and Harajuku. Start at the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing — observe the organized chaos from the Starbucks Reserve Roastery Shibuya (world's largest, 6 floors) or the Mag's Park rooftop. Visit Shibuya Sky observation deck for aerial views of the crossing and Tokyo skyline. Explore the newly developed Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Scramble Square complex — showcasing Tokyo's urban regeneration and architectural innovation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Harajuku. Visit the tranquil Meiji Jingu Shrine — a forested Shinto sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a profound spiritual counterpoint to the surrounding urban energy. Explore the shrine's inner garden and the Treasure Museum. Then browse Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's most sophisticated shopping boulevard lined with flagship stores designed by world-renowned architects (Prada by Herzog & de Meuron, Louis Vuitton by Jun Aoki, etc.).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Aoyama/Omotesando area — one of Tokyo's most upscale dining neighborhoods. Explore the quiet backstreets of Minami-Aoyama for cocktail bars and gallery spaces.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium bakery stop — Maison Landemaine Tokyo (Omotesando) for French-Japanese viennoiserie and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Omotesando Hills or Tokyu Plaza Omotesando Harajuku food floors — try Afuri ramen for yuzu-infused premium ramen, or a refined Japanese curry at Go Go Curry premium branch; budget ¥3,000–¥6,000
meals.dinner: Narisawa (2 Michelin stars, Minami-Aoyama) — one of Asia's best restaurants, celebrated for its 'innovative Satoyama cuisine' blending Japanese philosophy with French technique; or L'Effervescence (1 Michelin star) for seasonal French-Japanese cuisine; budget ¥40,000–¥70,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is serene in the morning but can be busy on weekends — Monday should be more peaceful. Omotesando shops open around 11:00. Book Narisawa months in advance — one of Tokyo's hardest reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — Tokyo's most dynamic mega-district. Begin at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (free entry, opens 09:00) for sweeping views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — a magnificent 58-hectare garden blending French formal, English landscape, and Japanese garden styles, with late-blooming cherry varieties potentially still in flower in mid-April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Shinjuku's tech and consumer culture: visit Yodobashi Camera Akiba (or the Shinjuku branch) multi-story electronics complex. Explore the narrow alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in daylight for atmosphere, then visit the Golden Gai district's unique micro-bar architecture. Browse Takashimaya Times Square department store's premium floors and its extraordinary basement food hall (depachika).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's legendary nightlife district. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a sophisticated bar in the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (famous from 'Lost in Translation') on the 52nd floor. Dinner in Shinjuku's upscale restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium Japanese breakfast set at Shinjuku's Isetan department store depachika basement (opens 10:00) — fresh wagashi sweets, seasonal rice bowls
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style with premium bento from a nearby depachika, or a refined lunch at Shinjuku's Takashimaya department store restaurant floors — try Kyoto-style obanzai cuisine or a premium soba set; budget ¥5,000–¥10,000
meals.dinner: Kozue (Park Hyatt Tokyo, 40th floor) — contemporary Japanese kaiseki with panoramic Shinjuku views, or Sushi Sawada (3 Michelin stars, nearby Ginza) for the pinnacle of Edo-mae sushi; budget ¥30,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entry fee and prohibits alcohol. The Metropolitan Government Building observation is free but check for closure days. New York Bar has a cover charge in the evening — worth every yen for the atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approx. 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa) — a UNESCO World Heritage mountain town housing the extraordinarily ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, the mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Arrive by 10:00 and spend the morning exploring the gilded shrine buildings, the famous Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight), and the surrounding cedar forest paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: visit Rinno-ji Temple with its impressive Sanbutsudo hall housing three giant gilded Buddha statues, walk the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River, and explore the quieter Futarasan Shrine. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Waterfall — one of Japan's most spectacular falls, plunging 97 meters into a gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by Limited Express (arriving approximately 19:00–20:00). Light dinner near Tsukiji or Ginza upon return — something simple but refined after a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Nikko — ensure a substantial meal as the journey is long
meals.lunch: Traditional Nikko cuisine at a local restaurant near the shrine complex — try yuba (tofu skin) dishes, a Nikko specialty, at Gyoshintei restaurant set within a historic garden; budget ¥5,000–¥8,000
meals.dinner: Return dinner at a Ginza or Tsukiji neighborhood restaurant — Ginza Kojyu (3 Michelin stars) for refined kaiseki if energy allows, or a premium soba dinner at Ginza Kojyu's more casual neighbor; budget ¥15,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Tobu Railway's 'Nikko All Area Pass' for unlimited transport within Nikko. Start early (depart by 07:30–08:00) to maximize time. Nikko can be chilly in April — bring layers. The shrine complex requires several hours to explore properly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the cutting-edge Odaiba artificial island — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront district showcasing Japan's vision of technology and urban innovation. Visit teamLab's second venue if not visited earlier, or explore the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robots, space exploration exhibits, and Japan's latest technological achievements. The museum's Geo-Cosmos — a massive LED globe displaying real-time Earth data — is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on Odaiba: visit the Toyota Mega Web (automotive technology showcase and test drive experiences), the DiverCity Tokyo Plaza with its life-sized Gundam statue (a cultural landmark of Japanese pop-tech culture), and the teamLab Digital Art Museum if not yet visited. Enjoy the views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo Bay from Odaiba Marine Park.
day_by_day.evening: Take the scenic Yurikamome automated monorail back toward central Tokyo, enjoying elevated views of the bay and city skyline at dusk. Dinner in the Shiodome/Shimbashi area — a sleek business district with excellent high-rise dining options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast, then grab a premium convenience store breakfast experience — Japanese 7-Eleven and Lawson offer surprisingly high-quality onigiri, sandwiches, and coffee that are a cultural experience in themselves
meals.lunch: Odaiba lunch at Aqua City or DiverCity mall's premium restaurant floors — try a refined Japanese hamburger steak (hambagu) at Kua'aina, or fresh seafood at a bay-view restaurant; budget ¥3,000–¥6,000
meals.dinner: Conrad Tokyo (Shiodome) — Cerise by Pierre Gagnaire for innovative French cuisine with Tokyo Bay panoramas, or the hotel's Japanese restaurant Kazahana for premium kaiseki; budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed Tuesdays. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a highlight — sit at the front for driver's-eye views. Odaiba can be windy off the bay — bring a jacket. Book Conrad Tokyo dinner well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the refined neighborhoods of Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish and cultured residential districts. Begin at Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — an architectural masterpiece and cultural institution combining a premium bookstore, music library, Anjin vintage magazine archive, and artisan coffee in a beautifully landscaped complex. Browse the curated selection of design, photography, art, and travel books.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Meguro River canal in Nakameguro — lined with boutiques, galleries, concept stores, and cafés housed in converted warehouses. Visit the Log Road Daikanyama for curated lifestyle brands. Explore the independent fashion and design boutiques that define Tokyo's avant-garde style culture. Visit the Hillside Terrace complex — a pioneering mixed-use development by architect Fumihiko Maki that helped define the neighborhood's character.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ebisu for the evening. Visit Yebisu Garden Place — a beautifully designed complex built on the historic Sapporo Brewery site, featuring the Yebisu Beer Museum and the Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon housed in a French château transported from Paris.

meals.breakfast: Premium breakfast at Daikanyama T-Site's Ivy Place restaurant — an all-day dining spot in a beautiful garden setting offering Japanese and Western breakfast options; budget ¥3,000–¥5,000
meals.lunch: Nakameguro canal-side lunch at Log Road's premium café or a neighborhood bistro — try Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku (Nakameguro branch) for artisan rice balls, or a refined pasta at a boutique Italian restaurant in the area; budget ¥4,000–¥7,000
meals.dinner: Château Restaurant Joël Robuchon (Ebisu, 2 Michelin stars) — the legendary French chef's Tokyo outpost in a stunning château setting, offering the pinnacle of French haute cuisine; budget ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person for the full tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Daikanyama and Nakameguro are best explored slowly on foot. Most boutiques open around 11:00–12:00. The Meguro River walk is particularly beautiful in late afternoon light. Book Joël Robuchon months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (approx. 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Arrive by 09:30 and begin at the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — the iconic 13.35-meter bronze Amida Buddha statue, one of Japan's most recognizable cultural icons. Explore the surrounding Zen temple grounds and walk through the bamboo groves of Hokoku-ji Temple (the 'Bamboo Temple') for a serene, otherworldly experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's network of Zen temples: visit Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji — two of the most important Rinzai Zen temples in Japan, set in forested mountain valleys. Hike a portion of the Daibutsu Hiking Course through ancient cedar forest connecting several historic sites. Browse the charming Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, ceramics, and traditional sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:30–19:00. Relaxed evening near the hotel — perhaps a quiet dinner in the Ginza/Tsukiji neighborhood to wind down before the final days.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Kamakura lunch at Hachinoki — a celebrated kaiseki restaurant set in a traditional Zen-style garden near Kencho-ji Temple, serving refined vegetarian shojin ryori (Buddhist temple cuisine) and seasonal Japanese courses; budget ¥8,000–¥15,000
meals.dinner: Return to Ginza for a relaxed dinner — Sushi Kanesaka (2 Michelin stars) for premier Edo-mae omakase sushi, or a refined teppanyaki dinner at Ginza Ukai-tei for premium Wagyu beef and seafood; budget ¥25,000–¥45,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is very popular on weekends — depart early to beat crowds. The Daibutsu Hiking Course takes 1.5–2 hours. Comfortable walking shoes essential. Book Hachinoki in advance. JR Pass covers the train journey.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the penultimate morning to a curated luxury shopping experience in Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district, steps from the hotel. Visit the Ginza Six complex (the largest commercial facility in Ginza) for its extraordinary mix of luxury brands, Japanese designers, a rooftop garden, and a basement art gallery. Explore the Itoya stationery flagship — a 12-story temple to premium paper, pens, and design goods unlike anything elsewhere in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artizon Museum (formerly Bridgestone Museum) in Nihonbashi — one of Tokyo's finest private art museums housing an exceptional collection of Impressionist, Post-Impressionist, and Japanese Western-style paintings. The stunning Nikken Sekkei-designed building is itself a work of architectural art. Afterward, explore the historic Nihonbashi neighborhood — Tokyo's original commercial heart, now home to beautifully preserved Meiji-era buildings alongside modern architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Tokyo — make it extraordinary. Return to a neighborhood or restaurant that resonated most during the trip, or try one final bucket-list dining experience. Consider a sake tasting experience at a premium sake bar in Ginza or Nihonbashi, exploring Japan's national beverage with expert guidance.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast or brunch at a Ginza luxury hotel — try the Palace Hotel Tokyo's Crown restaurant for a premium Sunday brunch with views of the Imperial Palace gardens
meals.lunch: Ginza Six's premium restaurant floors — try Ginza Kojyu's lunch course (more accessible than dinner), or a refined tempura lunch at Tempura Kondo (2 Michelin stars, Ginza) where the chef's seasonal vegetable tempura is legendary; budget ¥15,000–¥25,000
meals.dinner: Quintessential final dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (if reservations secured through hotel concierge months in advance — the world's most famous sushi restaurant) or Ginza Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) for a transcendent farewell omakase; budget ¥40,000–¥80,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sukiyabashi Jiro is notoriously difficult to book — only possible through hotel concierge with connections, and only for serious sushi enthusiasts. Have backup reservations confirmed. Ginza Six rooftop garden is free and lovely on a clear spring afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — keep it relaxed and meaningful. Take one last walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market at dawn (06:30–08:00) to say farewell to the neighborhood that has been home base for the trip. Pick up premium food souvenirs: vacuum-packed dashi stock, premium soy sauce, wasabi, matcha powder, and artisan pickles. Visit the nearby Namiyoke Inari Shrine — a small but important shrine dedicated to protecting the Tsukiji market community, offering a quiet moment of reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final packing, hotel checkout. Transfer to airport via private luxury limousine service (allow 2–3 hours before international departure). At the airport, explore the premium duty-free shopping at Narita or Haneda — both offer excellent selections of Japanese whisky (Yamazaki, Hibiki), sake, premium cosmetics, and food gifts unavailable elsewhere.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo — carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring the world's most sophisticated city through its food, technology, art, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Tsukiji — a bowl of fresh tuna sashimi don (tuna rice bowl) and miso soup at Tsukiji Sushizanmai, or a standing sushi breakfast at one of the outer market's top vendors; a perfect final meal in Tokyo
meals.lunch: Airport lunch — Narita and Haneda both have excellent premium dining options including ramen, sushi, and tonkatsu; try ANA's premium lounge if eligible, or a last ramen at Fuunji's airport branch
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Tokyo traffic on Monday mornings can be heavy. Narita Airport requires 90 minutes minimum before departure; Haneda is closer (45–60 minutes from central Tokyo). Purchase any remaining souvenirs at the airport's extensive duty-free. Confirm all purchased food items comply with customs regulations of your destination country.
